notable_absence.finding: Consistent with every other SELECT-family page in this round: no management-plane capella-role:* gate, only the data-plane credential-type privilege pair. This page also states the degenerate case explicitly - 'To execute the following statement, the user does not need any special privileges' for `SELECT 1` (a keyspace-free query) - reinforcing that the privilege requirement attaches to the keyspaces referenced, not to the SELECT statement as such.

cross_component_finding: Two findings: (1) Recurrence of the known issue in docs-issues/capella-pages-cite-server-versions.json - 'In clusters running Couchbase Server 7.6 or later, the projection is returned in the order specified by the query. In prior versions, the projection was sorted alphabetically.' is a literal 'Couchbase Server' version-gate citation on a Capella page. (2) The page's RBAC Examples subsection describes per-keyspace access requirements using a different doc path than the credential-type table above it - it links '[read](../../clusters/manage-database-users.md#about-database-user-permissions) access to `airline`' rather than the cluster-rbac.md#cluster-access-credential-types path used by the Prerequisites table just above. Both describe what appears to be the same 'Read' privilege concept, but are sourced from two different pages (cluster-rbac.md vs. manage-database-users.md) without cross-linking each other on this page - a minor internal inconsistency in how the docs point readers to the authoritative privilege reference, though not modeled as a separate relation since the underlying concept (privilege:capella-basic-access-read) is the same.
